text:
Anya Venkataraman: quick follow-up from the CP separation RFC — we need a pragmatic migration plan for DNS + cert propagation when we introduce per-tenant controlplane endpoints (cp-v2). main constraints: avoid long downtime for tenants with high TTLs, handle certs for on-prem customers that pull certs via our agent, and keep rollback path to cp-v1 easy.
Samir Patel: +1. can you spell out the rollout steps you have in mind? curious about how we avoid TTL-related traffic hitting old cp endpoints during cutover.
Anya Venkataraman: sketch: 1) create canary hostnames for each tenant: `cp-v2-canary.<tenant>.rnw` (low TTL), 2) deploy cp-v2 behind those hostnames, 3) validate health/metrics for subset, 4) start phased DNS split by updating resolver entries to point to cp-v2 with short TTLs, 5) for long-TTL tenants, use an edge proxy that rewrites SNI to cp-v2 when we detect canary header, 6) once stable, lower the old records' priority and eventually swap canonical CNAMEs.
Jin Park: edge-rewrite sounds heavy. ops concerns: 1) operator path for on-prem (agents) — they cache CA roots and certs. we need a mechanism to push new CA or intermediate without touching agent config. 2) cert rotation window: some tenants rotate certs infrequently.
Anya Venkataraman: for agents we propose a CA-signal channel: agents poll `agent-control-channel` and accept signed bundle envelopes. plan: ship a new bundle with cross-signed intermediate that v2 certs chain to. agents will accept both old and new CA for 72h. that buys us a coexistence window.
Samir Patel: sounds good. how do we validate agent acceptance at scale? we can't query every customer agent synchronously.
Anya Venkataraman: we add an opt-in canary flag per tenant that triggers the agent to log an acceptance event to our onboarding-telemetry topic. for non-opt-in, we rely on traffic signals + TCP-level connection success rates via edge metrics.
Jin Park: rollback story? if cp-v2 has issues, how do we fail back safely without cert mismatch?
Anya Venkataraman: keep cp-v1 certs valid until rollback window closes. plan: dual-cert presentation on v2 endpoints (present v2 cert normally, but present v1 cert for clients that SNI-match cp-v1). the edge proxy can present fallback identity based on SNI. this lets us revert DNS entries while maintaining TLS handshakes.
Samir Patel: dual-cert/TLS trickery might complicate ALB/ELB setups. do we have infra support?
Jin Park: ALBs don't support dual cert per SNI variant easily. we can do it with a small HAProxy fleet in front for canary slice only. heavier but limited scope.
Anya Venkataraman: exactly — only for canary/rollback slices. full rollout uses standard ALB once old clients have rotated.
deploy-bot: deployment cp-v2/region-us-west-2 canary group started at 1743214350 — smoke tests queued. :rocket:
Samir Patel: ok let's put an ops runbook in next steps: - list tenants with TTL > 300s - enable canary flag for 5% low-traffic tenants - deploy HAProxy canary frontends + dual-cert - push cross-signed intermediate to agents - monitor SNI/TLS rejects and connect success.
Anya Venkataraman: will write runbook + include rollback playbook (DNS revert + remove cross-signing if needed). will post PR to docs and tag infra/ops. any objections?
Jin Park: no objections. add a step to test on-prem agents behind NAT/proxy — edge cases.
Samir Patel: and add a metric for cert-chain-acceptance rate per-tenant. we need an alert threshold.
Anya Venkataraman: noted. I'll include alert thresholds and a short checklist for infra to stand up HAProxy canaries.
Samir Patel: thanks — ping me on the PR for the runbook review.
Anya Venkataraman: will do. :thumbsup:
